definitions.explanation: Describes behavior or manner that is off-putting or unpleasant.
Often used to describe sexually suggestive or inappropriate behavior.

examples.japanese: いやらしい⟦{言|い}い{方|かた}→言い方：14165_iikata⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧な。
examples.english: Don't say it in such a nasty way.

examples.japanese: いやらしい⟦{笑|わら}い→笑う：00685_warau⟧⟦{方|かた}→方：10665_kata⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{気|き}になる→気になる：03027_kininaru⟧。
examples.english: His unpleasant way of laughing bothers me.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{態度|たいど}→態度：03396_taido⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧いやらしいほど⟦{丁寧|ていねい}→丁寧：00896_teinei⟧だった。
いやらしい⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{見|み}ないで→見る：00283_miru⟧。
examples.english: Don't look at me with those lewd eyes.

examples.japanese: いやらしい⟦{冗談|じょうだん}→冗談：03347_joudan⟧はやめて⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{映画|えいが}→映画：02273_eiga⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧いやらしい⟦シーン→シーン：08914_shiin⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: That movie has a lot of indecent scenes.

notes:
いやらしい has two main senses: generally unpleasant/nasty behavior, and sexually suggestive or vulgar behavior. The sexual connotation is very common, so use with caution.

WRITING:
Usually written in hiragana. Also written as ⟦{嫌|いや}→嫌：10232_iya⟧らしい.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- いやらしい⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧: lewd eyes, suggestive gaze
- いやらしい⟦{言|い}い{方|かた}→言い方：14165_iikata⟧: nasty way of speaking
- いやらしい⟦{笑|わら}い→笑う：00685_warau⟧⟦{方|かた}→方：10665_kata⟧: unpleasant/creepy laugh
- いやらしい⟦{冗談|じょうだん}→冗談：03347_joudan⟧: dirty joke

USAGE:
When describing a person's gaze or behavior, the sexual connotation (sense 2) is often the default interpretation. When describing speech or manner, sense 1 (unpleasant, underhanded) may apply.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{卑猥|ひわい}→卑猥：18986_hiwai⟧: obscene, indecent (more formal, stronger)
- ⟦{下品|げひん}→下品：00060_gehin⟧: vulgar, crude (focuses on lack of refinement)
- ⟦{嫌|いや}→嫌：10232_iya⟧: unpleasant (general dislike, without sexual nuance)
